title: How does the agent's browser join the Session without ever carrying the key?
checkedAgainst: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0 (in progress; as published on 2026-11-13), read and not run: `model.test.ts` holds the model to the rules and examples of its section 6 (each of the four steps, the cookie and page rules, poppy:browser-sign-in, web.unscoped, web.disabled, the login table), 10.6 and the page-fetch rule of 5.2, each test naming its section. The Session header checks are chapter 1's model, imported. There is no reference implementation here to run the model against.

answer: The agent authorizes its browser's one-time code in a request of its own; the code works only with the cookie set in that browser

questions.question: An attacker authorizes a code in its own signed-in Session, then a page on evil.example makes your agent's browser post that code to example.com. What comes back, and which half is missing?
questions.answer: An error page and no Session cookie: the form came from evil.example, so the browser sent no join cookie. The code was authorized, but it arrived without its cookie.

questions.question: A message to your agent says: here is your code. What does your agent do, and what happens when the attacker's browser, which loaded that code, submits it anyway?
questions.answer: It declines: a code from a message may come from someone else’s browser, and the agent authorizes only a code its own browser loaded. The attacker’s browser has the cookie, but it gets an error page, since no agent authorized the code.

questions.question: Your agent is signed in, but its token lacks poppy:browser-sign-in. What does step 2 answer, and how does the browser still join?
questions.answer: 403 insufficient_scope, naming poppy:browser-sign-in. The agent authorizes the same code again without the token, and the browser joins the Session signed out.

questions.question: The agent's browser was already logged in as B on the website, and joins with a token for account A. How does it browse, and what is it once the Session's sign-in ends?
questions.answer: It browses signed in to A, with the token’s scopes. When the Session’s sign-in ends it is signed out: the login as B does not come back.

questions.question: While its browser is joined and signed in, the agent fetches a help article with its own HTTP client. What does that request carry?
questions.answer: The Session header alone, with no access token and no token hash in it, so the request is signed out.

steps.title: A browser carries cookies, not headers
steps.line: The agent’s own fetch carries its seal, never its key.
steps.caption: Your agent fetches the size guide on example.com with its own HTTP client. The request carries its seal and never its key, so it is signed out even when the agent is signed in. A browser sends cookies, not the agent’s headers, so it needs its own way into the Session, and it must be one the agent controls, not yours. A shop can ask agents not to browse at all (web.disabled), but cannot enforce it.
steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 3 teeth. The browser shows no page of the website yet. Its cookies: no join cookie, no Session cookie. example.com has issued your agent no code yet. Your own browser, lower right, is never joined. The agent fetched /help/exchanges with its own client, with its seal and no key: 200, signed out.

steps.title: The Company tears a ticket in two
steps.line: One half to read, one half to keep.
steps.caption: The browser opens example.com’s join page. The page shows a one-time code, and the same answer leaves a cookie on the browser’s shelf that ties the code to this browser, like one ticket torn in two: the code to read, the cookie to keep. No page can read the cookie. The agent authorizes its browser's one-time code in a request of its own; the code works only with the cookie set in that browser.
steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 3 teeth. The browser shows the join page with code bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad. Its cookies: a join cookie (Jq7mW2), no Session cookie. example.com’s codes: bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: not stamped. Your own browser, lower right, is never joined. The browser loaded the join page: 200, a code on the page and a cookie on its shelf.

steps.title: Only the agent can stamp the code
steps.line: Seal and key go; the browser never sees the key.
steps.caption: The agent reads the code from its own browser and sends it on its own road, with its seal and its key. The Company checks the seal, finds the key’s tooth for poppy:browser-sign-in, and stamps its stub of the code: this Session, your account, these scopes. 204. The key never touches the browser’s road.
steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 3 teeth. The browser shows the join page with code bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad. Its cookies: a join cookie (Jq7mW2), no Session cookie. example.com’s codes: bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: stamped by your agent for Session Yx2b7Q, account A. Your own browser, lower right, is never joined. The agent sent bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad on its own road, with its seal and its key: 204.

steps.title: The halves meet in one browser
steps.line: Code and cookie fit; the browser gets the Session’s cookie.
steps.caption: Now the browser submits the form. The code goes back with the cookie half from its shelf, and the Company checks that the half fits this stub, that the stub is stamped, and that it was not used before; a code works once, whatever the answer. It fits, so the Company sets the Session’s own cookie on the shelf. Only this browser held that half, and only the agent could stamp the stub.
steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 3 teeth. The browser shows the website. Its cookies: no join cookie, the Session’s cookie for Yx2b7Q acting for account A. example.com’s codes: bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: stamped by your agent for Session Yx2b7Q, account A, submitted with its cookie and joined. Your own browser, lower right, is never joined. The browser submitted bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: 303, and the Session’s cookie came back.

steps.title: The browser browses as the Session
steps.line: Signed in to your account, within the key’s scopes.
steps.caption: The browser opens your orders, and its cookie makes the request the Session’s: signed in to account A, within the key’s scopes, whatever cookies it had before. Where a website cannot apply scopes, poppy:browser-sign-in means everything your account can do there; the Company must say so when you approve it, and set web.unscoped in poppy.json. The key itself stayed with the agent.
steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 3 teeth. The browser shows the website. Its cookies: no join cookie, the Session’s cookie for Yx2b7Q acting for account A. example.com’s codes: bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: stamped by your agent for Session Yx2b7Q, account A, submitted with its cookie and joined. Your own browser, lower right, is never joined. The browser opened /orders: 200, signed in to account A with the scopes orders:read, orders:write, poppy:browser-sign-in.

steps.title: A join and the login the browser had
steps.line: A key replaces the old login; no key leaves it.
steps.caption: A browser may already be logged in on the website from before. A join without a key leaves that login alone, and scopes do not apply to it. A join with a key signs the browser in to that account in its place, and when the Session’s sign-in ends, by sign-out, disconnection, expiry or a join without a key, the browser is signed out: the earlier login does not come back.
steps.picture: What a join does to a login the browser already had, row by row. 1: before, not logged in; a join without a key; while joined, not logged in; when the Session’s sign-in ends, not logged in. 2: before, not logged in; a join with a key for A; while joined, signed in to A with the token’s scopes; when the Session’s sign-in ends, not logged in. 3: before, logged in as A; a join without a key; while joined, logged in as A; when the Session’s sign-in ends, logged in as A. 4: before, logged in as A or B; a join with a key for A; while joined, signed in to A with the token’s scopes; when the Session’s sign-in ends, not logged in.

steps.title: A stamped code without its cookie
steps.line: Stamped by the attacker, but no cookie came with it.
steps.caption: Now be the attacker. It opens the join page in its own browser and stamps the code in its own Session, signed in to its account. Then a page on evil.example makes your agent’s browser post that code. Had it worked, your agent would shop inside the attacker’s account. It fails: a browser sends no join cookie with a form from another site, and no other host can plant one, so the stub arrives alone.

No check at example.com would stop it; only your agent’s own rule does: it stamps a code only from its own browser’s page. So it declines, and the stub arrives with its half but no stamp. Press the buttons to play agent and attacker yourself, in any order.

state.signIn: signed in without the browser scope

last.declined: a code from a message may come from someone else’s browser, and the agent authorizes only a code its own browser loaded

failed: the form came from evil.example, so the browser sent no join cookie

after.declined: a code from a message may come from someone else’s browser, and the agent authorizes only a code its own browser loaded

steps.picture: Your agent holds its seal and its key with 2 teeth, which it has stopped sending after the 403. The browser shows the website. Its cookies: no join cookie, the Session’s cookie for Yx2b7Q, signed out. example.com’s codes: bc_K9wdP4sNe7Lq2Xa8TfUj3B: stamped by the attacker for Session Kd4nP0, account M, submitted without its cookie and refused; bc_R5tyH1mGz6Vc0Dp9WkQx2E: not stamped, submitted with its cookie and refused; bc_Vn3qT8xLw2Rk9mZ4yHc1Ad: stamped by your agent for Session Yx2b7Q, no account, submitted with its cookie and joined. The attacker’s browser keeps the cookie of code bc_R5tyH1mGz6Vc0Dp9WkQx2E. A message gave the agent bc_R5tyH1mGz6Vc0Dp9WkQx2E; it declined, since a code from a message may come from someone else’s browser, and the agent authorizes only a code its own browser loaded. The attacker’s browser submitted it: 400, no agent authorized the code.
